transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess… mostly my sleep. It’s been bad for a long time. I’m exhausted when I go to bed, but I keep waking up at every little noise, and then I’m up too early feeling like I didn’t really sleep.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say anxious exactly. Maybe tense sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Do you feel tired or fatigued during the day?

Yeah… I do. By the time I’m done seeing my home-health clients and then come back and help around the house, I just feel heavy. Even little things like charting notes or folding laundry feel like a lot to push through.
Do you often worry about things?
I mean… I think about things, sure. But I’m not sure I’d call it worrying all the time. It’s more just… stuff on my mind, I guess.
Do you have bad dreams or nightmares?
Not really nightmares, no. It’s more that my sleep is just… broken. I fall into bed worn out, but I wake up at every little sound, and then I’m up before the alarm feeling like I didn’t really sleep.
Do you feel anxious when you're lying in bed trying to fall asleep?
I don’t know… not really anxious, exactly. I’m usually just lying there trying to settle down. I haven’t noticed it as fear or panic or anything like that.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?
I’m not sure. I don’t think it’s like thoughts repeating over and over… not that I’ve really noticed.
Do you have thoughts that you feel compelled to act on?
No… I don’t think so. I don’t really feel like I have to act on anything like that.
Do you have thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I’m trying to push thoughts away on purpose… nothing that stands out to me.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to?
I mean… I worry sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s for no reason. It’s hard to say. Nothing specific comes to mind.
Do you have thoughts that intrude into your mind and are difficult to get rid of?
I don’t think so… not in a way that feels like that. I have thoughts on my mind sometimes, but I wouldn’t say they intrude or that I can’t get rid of them.
Do you find that you're awake and alert at the same time every day, regardless of when you go to bed?
Yeah… kind of. Even if I go to bed later, I still wake up early, before the alarm usually. I don’t feel very rested. The sleep is pretty broken.
Do you find it difficult to fall asleep and stay asleep when you try to sleep at a later time than your usual wake-up time?

Yeah… if I try to shift my sleep later, it doesn’t really work. I might fall into bed exhausted, but I wake up at every little noise, and then I’m still up early before the alarm. It doesn’t feel like I really slept.
Do you find yourself waking up and going to bed at the same times every day, even on weekends or days off?
Yeah… mostly. I tend to go to bed worn out, but then I wake up at little sounds and I’m up before the alarm anyway. Weekends don’t really change it much. I just don’t feel rested.
Do you feel like you have to wake up at the same time every day, no matter what?
I guess it feels that way, yeah. Even when I don’t mean to, I’m up before the alarm. I wake at little sounds, and then I just… don’t feel like I rested.
Do you think your body has a natural wake-up time that it tries to follow every day?
Yeah… it seems like it. Even if I’m worn out, I wake up to little sounds, and then I’m up before the alarm. It’s like my body just won’t really let me rest.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you could sleep in later and wake up at a more traditional time?

I don’t know… maybe a little, but it’s not really just the time. I fall into bed exhausted, then I wake up at every little sound, and by the time I’m up before the alarm, I feel like I didn’t really sleep.
Do you usually wake up feeling more rested on days when you can sleep in later?
Not really. Even if I can stay in bed longer, I still wake up at every little sound… and then I feel like I didn’t really rest anyway.
Do you feel like you would have trouble adjusting to a significantly different sleep schedule?

I think so… yeah. My sleep’s already pretty broken. I can be exhausted and still wake up at every little sound, then I’m up before the alarm anyway. So changing the schedule much would probably be hard.
Do you typically wake up early because you feel rested or because you can't sleep anymore?
Because I can’t sleep anymore, I guess. I don’t wake up feeling rested… I’m just awake before the alarm, and it feels like I barely slept.
